representation: A unit reference square at the origin, its image under the matrix A = [[a,b],[0,1]] drawn as the parallelogram whose two sides are the matrix columns, with arrows for the images of e1 and e2.
entities: x-axis and y-axis through the origin at (330,360)
arrow e1 from origin to column 1 (a, 0)
arrow e2 from origin to column 2 (b, 1)
two remaining parallelogram edges (top and right)
motion: A blend parameter s = t/6 morphs every image vertex from the identity position (1-s)v + s*Mv, so the square visibly becomes the parallelogram in 6 s; sliders a and b change the target matrix and the morph restarts from identity on reload.
checkpoints: 0.1 s: identity -> matrix, reference square stated
2 s: the two arrow tips are the columns
4 s: what a and b each do, rows not elementwise
5.9 s: area = |det A| = |a|, shear keeps area, a = 0 would collapse
misconceptionTest: Checkpoint 3 states the output is x' = a x + b y with y' = y, so entries mix coordinates rather than multiplying matching ones; and the parallelogram visibly moves, refuting 'the transformed grid is unchanged'. Area claim is only made where det = a is exactly true.
accessibility: Alt text distinguishes reference square from image parallelogram; both sliders keyboard operable; every claim is also in text (columns, rows, area), not colour; reducedMotion no-autoplay.
